title: Understanding AUTOINCREMENT
learning_outcomes: Describe the main purpose and behavior of understanding autoincrement.

content.intro: This lesson covers understanding autoincrement as part of SQLite’s embedded relational database model. Work through one small example, verify the output, and then connect the result to the listed subtopics from the supplied curriculum.
content.why_it_matters: Application validation improves feedback; schema constraints protect all writers.

items.title: Automatic row-ID assignment
items.text: A plain `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` already allocates unused rowids. `AUTOINCREMENT` adds bookkeeping to prevent reuse of previously issued rowids, which adds overhead; use it only when that guarantee is required.

items.title: The AUTOINCREMENT keyword

items.title: Storage and performance trade-offs
items.text: A plain `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` already allocates unused rowids. `AUTOINCREMENT` adds bookkeeping to prevent reuse of previously issued rowids, which adds overhead; use it only when that guarantee is required.

items.title: When ordinary integer primary keys are sufficient
items.text: In a rowid table, a column declared exactly `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` aliases the rowid. Composite keys, `WITHOUT ROWID`, and types such as `INT PRIMARY KEY` have different behavior; do not infer identity semantics from a column name.
